chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about Al-Khaluq, 'Do I take from it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it, but I do not like that you remain perpetually upon it.'

key_terms.الْخَلُوق: Al-Khaluq, a specific type of perfume or scent used in the Arabian Peninsula.
key_terms.تَدُومَ عَلَيْهِ: Tadumma 'alayhi, meaning to remain perpetually or constantly upon it.
key_terms.لَا أُحِبُّ: La uhibbu, indicating a preferred dislike or karahah (not forbidden but discouraged).
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: La ba'sa, indicating permissibility or that there is no religious objection.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the continuous use of perfume according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Zurara asked Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the permissibility of using Al-Khaluq (a type of perfume or scent). The Imam ruled that it is permissible (la ba'sa), but expressed a preference (karahah) against its constant, perpetual use. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance between absolute prohibition (haram) and recommended dislike (mustahabb al-tark), suggesting that while the scent is lawful, moderation is spiritually preferred to avoid ostentation or excessive attachment to worldly adornments.
